subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: surge corridor, autoscale leash & SOW for BridgePoint Health
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@bridgepointhealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@bridgepointhealth.com
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: surge corridor, autoscale leash & SOW for BridgePoint Health

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking the call last week. Quick recap of BridgePoint's constraints and asks so we can get a SOW out:

- Current production inference baseline: ~16 A100-equivalent GPUs (steady-state).
- Expected weekly peak windows: short spikes to ~40–48 GPUs (30–90 minutes) for evening batch transforms and model refresh jobs.
- We need predictable pricing for baseline, a managed approach for transients (we can tolerate lower QoS during peak), and clarity on eviction behavior if Redwood needs to reclaim capacity.
- Compliance: audit logs for all model requests and KV cache retention policy.
- Ops ask: documentable runbook and an SLA for baseline.

Primary questions:
1) Can Redwood support a "surge corridor" to 48 GPUs with a policy that prioritizes baseline traffic and gracefully sheds non-critical batch jobs?
2) How would you bill surge usage (metered bursts, credits, or committed shoulder pool)?
3) Is there a prewarm strategy to avoid cold-start latency when you scale up for scheduled batch runs?

If you can share a short SOW + capacity model (spreadsheet) and a proposed autoscale policy I can circulate to procurement and ops. We target signing in the next 10 business days.

Thanks,
Alex Rivera
Head of ML Ops | BridgePoint Health
alex.rivera@bridgepointhealth.com

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@bridgepointhealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: surge corridor, autoscale leash & SOW for BridgePoint Health

Alex — thanks for the clear summary. Long version below; tl;dr: yes, we can do a managed surge corridor + predictable billing using a hybrid model (committed baseline + shoulder pool + metered transient), and we'll include a prewarm/predictive autoscale policy in the SOW.

On Mon, 4 Jun 2028 at 09:12 AM Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@bridgepointhealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks for taking the call last week. Quick recap...

Proposal outline (operational + commercial):

1) Capacity topology
- Baseline slab (committed): 16 GPUs — reserved and SLA-backed (99.9% availability).
- Shoulder pool (soft-commit): 12 GPUs — prioritized for baseline owners but preemptible with 30 minutes notice; billed at a discounted shoulder rate.
- Surge corridor (transient): up to +20 GPUs (total up to 48) available as metered burst capacity for scheduled batch windows or opportunistic spikes. This tranche is preemptible and subject to the eviction leash described below.

2) Autoscale & prewarm strategy ("tempo guardband")
- Predictive prewarm: for scheduled batch windows we use the customer's runbook schedule or webhook triggers to instantiate instances with a 20-minute prewarm.
- Telemetry-driven prewarm: if observed short-term request rate rising >25% above baseline for 5 minutes, we attempt a fast-scale to the surge corridor (subject to available capacity).
- Progressive ramp: scale in 3 steps (baseline -> shoulder -> surge) to avoid spiky resource churn.

3) Eviction behavior ("eviction leash")
- Non-critical batch jobs are marked with a "evictable" tag. When capacity reclamation is required, evictable jobs receive a 5-minute drain signal and are routed to a lower-cost model variant or queued for retry.
- Critical inference traffic (baseline tenants) is never preempted without a 30-minute notice and a recorded incident.

4) Billing & credits
- Baseline slab: committed monthly fee (standard SOW rates).
- Shoulder pool: hourly discounted reclaimable fee; usage up to the shoulder size billed at shoulder rate.
- Transient surge: metered per-GPU-minute at the burst rate. First calendar quarter after go-live: we provide a one-time pool of 1000 GPU-minutes of burst credits to smooth first-month variability.

5) Compliance & telemetry
- We'll enable request-level audit logs and KV cache retention controls (configurable retention window). Logs will be available via the Redwood Console and can be exported to your SIEM.

6) Runbook & support
- We'll include a draft ops-playbook with escalation paths, on-call handoffs, and canary deploy windows. Dedicated oncall for initial 90-day ramp.

Next steps
- Internal ops: Marissa, can you draft SOW language and a capacity model (spreadsheet) capturing the committed vs shoulder vs burst tranches?
- Karthik, pls add any guardrails on eviction thresholds we should include in the SOW.
- Alex: once we share the draft SOW I'll flag the procurement items (DocuSign link, commercial terms).

Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to walk the SOW with BridgePoint ops.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@bridgepointhealth.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft SOW & capacity model (BridgePoint)

Alex / team — attaching an initial SOW and a capacity spreadsheet for your review. Highlights from the draft SOW:

- Section 2.1: Baseline (16 A100-equivalent GPUs) — SLA 99.9% availability, uptime measured at per-hour granularity.
- Section 2.2: Shoulder pool (12 GPUs) — soft-commit; reclaimable with 30-minute notice; billed at shoulder hourly rate.
- Section 2.3: Surge corridor — metered burst up to 48 total GPUs. Eviction leash: 5-minute drain + graceful fallback to lower model variant.
- Section 3.4: Prewarm windows — scheduled preheat (configurable, default 20 minutes) and telemetry triggers (25% sustained rise over 5 minutes).
- Appendix A: Ops runbook excerpt (attached as ops-playbook-dedicated.txt) including alerts and thresholds: CPU/GPU util >85% for 3 consecutive minutes triggers shoulder scale; queue depth >2000 triggers surge policy.

Attachments included:
- BridgePoint_Surge_SOW_v1.pdf (draft)
- capacity-model-bridgepoint.xlsx (spreadsheet with cost scenarios)
- ops-playbook-dedicated.txt (runbook excerpt and oncall matrix)

Marissa (ops) notes: we recommend a 4-week staged provisioning calendar: week 1 baseline racked & smoke tested; week 2 shoulder pool enabled; week 3 scheduled batch windows tested with prewarm; week 4 go-live and 90-day oncall.

Feedback welcome — I highlighted the procurement items that procurement will need to confirm (billing contact, PO terms, and security questionnaire).

— Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
